Subject: CAIQ evidence request: ephemeral logs and tokenization provenance

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the kickoff call earlier this week. As part of our CAIQ review we need to validate controls related to runtime logging and token handling (sections in the CAIQ that map to data lineage, telemetry, and crypto boundary tagging). Can you provide: 

- A short narrative describing how Redwood captures ephemeral inference logs (what is captured, where it lives, and who can access them).
- A small anonymized sample of ephemeral logs showing token indices and provenance fields (redact PII). CSV is fine.
- A mapping (spreadsheet) that ties the runtime log fields to specific CAIQ control IDs and the evidence artifact for each control.

We aim to close this item by next Wednesday (2026-09-23). If you have an internal owner for the artifacts and a timeline for upload to the shared drive, please include that.

Appreciate a short plan (1-2 bullets) so we can track scope on our side.

Best,
Alice Mercer
Security Assurance Lead
Skybridge Health Compliance

--

Subject: Re: CAIQ evidence request: ephemeral logs and tokenization provenance

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask. High level plan below and attached artifacts are staged in the Drive link (see manifest).

Plan (short):
- Today: provide a redacted CSV sample of ephemeral logs + tokenization_readme describing the provenance fields. (attached: ephemeral_logs_sample.csv, tokenization_readme.md)
- Tomorrow: deliver CAIQ mapping spreadsheet that links each runtime field to the CAIQ control, owner, and evidence path (attached draft: CAIQ_map_ephemeral_logs_v1.xlsx).
- Wednesday: finalize and upload a signed manifest and answer any follow-ups.

Narrative (concise):
Redwood captures ephemeral inference telemetry to support observability and security investigations; the logs include: request_id, model_variant, user_prompt_hash (one-way salted hash), token_index_range, token_source (user/system/cache), timestamp_utc, node_id, and trace_id. Raw user text is never stored in the ephemeral pipeline beyond short-lived in-memory buffers; persisted telemetry contains only hashed or bucketed representations to prevent re-identification. Access to persisted telemetry is restricted to the Security and Observability teams via role-based access and audited through our internal SIEM (control: evidence_id RED-OBS-LOG-2026).

Ownership and access: 
- Evidence owner: Marissa Cole (observability).
- Engineering contact for tokenization details: David Kim (runtime).

Uploading: I will upload the artifacts to the shared folder and paste the link below once the spreadsheet is finalized. We redacted PII and included a short readme explaining the redaction and sampling approach.

Attachments in this message: ephemeral_logs_sample.csv (CSV, redacted), tokenization_readme.md (TXT)

Thanks — let us know if you want a brief walkthrough call while you review.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Trust & Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Thanks Neha — this looks like the right approach. A couple of clarifying asks before you finalize the spreadsheet: 

1) Sampling window: can you confirm the time range used for the sample CSV and the retention policy applied for ephemeral logs (we want to note retention in the CAIQ annotation).
2) Token provenance: in the token_source field you mention "cache" — please confirm whether cache-origin tokens are attributable to prior user requests (i.e., do you store cache keys that could be linked back to user identifiers) or if cache keys are salted/hashed per-tenant.

If you can answer 1-2 inline in the spreadsheet notes and include a short scoped excerpt (one paragraph) about redaction/PII handling, we should be able to map to the CAIQ control about data minimization and retention.

Also, can Marissa and David confirm they can respond to follow-up technical artifact requests later this week?

Regards,
Alice
